scope: sixth falsification: even a 7-bit prologue with two fields decodes ONE field - the emerging theory is one field per snapshot
body: runs/snapshot-p7f2.bin (7-bit prologue, two [present(0)+delta] groups, terminator, 26 bits)
falsified_so_far: and the accepted single-field body itself measures exactly 29 bits
the_emerging_theory: the ps block writes EXACTLY ONE field per snapshot in this build

the disassembly supports it: after each decoded field the client runs `add [eax+0x3BA0],1` (ps count) and the loop bound is that same count, so the bound advances with the loop instead of limiting it - the loop exits on the has-ps bit instead, and in every body we send that bit arrives after one field

the field INDEX is not chosen by us either: the landing index comes from a slot index the client derives from that same count (`esi = edx*0x58`), so the CLIENT decides which field of the table is written on each snapshot
if that is true, a playerState is built up across MANY snapshots, one field each, and the server cannot target a field directly at all in a single body
why_this_ends_black_box_work: if the client chooses the field index itself, then constructing a body to write 'origin' is not a matter of getting the bits right - the index is out of our control
confirming or refuting that requires observing the index the client picks on a real sequence, which is a debugger observation, not a construction experiment
six hypotheses have been falsified with a probe that is now itself validated (0x670FF0 calls 0x6701D0 exactly once, confirmed in the disassembly), so the failure is in the model, not the instrument
what_would_settle_it: a debugger breakpoint at 0x471BB3 (where the slot/index is loaded) logging `[ebp-0xd0]`, `edi` and `esi` for each snapshot of a real sequence
or a captured real snapshot stream: the per-frame field indices would be visible in the decoded output
